CVE-2026-116128.title: Starlet versions from 0.20 before 0.33 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded buffering when decoding chunked request bodies
CVE-2026-116128.description:
Starlet versions from 0.20 before 0.33 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded buffering when decoding chunked request bodies.

The decoder adds each read to one buffer of unconsumed input. Nothing limits the length of a chunk-size line, so a line without a CRLF grows the buffer for as long as the client keeps sending, and the read timeout restarts after every read. The data of a large chunk is also held in the buffer until the whole chunk has arrived.

A remote attacker can exhaust a worker's memory with a single request.

CVE-2026-123865.title: Node.js is vulnerable to an HTTP/2 memory and file-descriptor leak via a protocol error during session shutdown
CVE-2026-123865.description: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can permanently leak Node.js server memory and file descriptors. If a peer triggers a protocol error, for example an oversized frame header, while the session is already shutting down, nghttp2 tears the session down internally but Node.js never notices, leaving a dangling session: the socket stays in CLOSE_WAIT and all of Node.js's HTTP/2 state for that connection is held in memory indefinitely, with no further cost to the attacker. The attacker can start the shutdown remotely by sending GOAWAY(NO_ERROR), so it is reliable against default HTTP/2 servers. It is an incomplete-fix case of CVE-2026-48937: that fix detected nghttp2 internal terminations by watching for GOAWAY sent while not shutting down, but missed terminations that arrive while the session is already shutting down. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via unrestricted upload of dangerous file types in the service ticket feature of the client panel. The application does not verify the type or name of files attached to service tickets. An authenticated attacker can upload an .htaccess file to bypass the access restrictions on the storage directory, together with a PHP script. Visiting the uploaded PHP file's URL leads to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the web server.

This issue was fixed in commit 89dd3f7.

CVE-2026-41428.description: Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.35.4, the authenticated middleware uses unanchored regular expressions to match public (no-auth) endpoint patterns against ctx.request.url. Since ctx.request.url in Koa includes the query string, an attacker can access any protected endpoint by appending a public endpoint path as a query parameter. For example, POST /api/global/users/search?x=/api/system/status bypasses all authentication because the regex /api/system/status/ matches in the query string portion of the URL. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.35.4.

CVE-2026-99209.title: drm/xe: skip eviction of a BO with no resource
CVE-2026-99209.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/xe: skip eviction of a BO with no resource

xe_evict_flags() switches on tbo->resource->mem_type to choose an
eviction placement. An xe BO can reach eviction with no ttm.resource,
e.g. an imported dma-buf BO whose resource was freed during teardown
while its attachment is still live: the exporter then invalidates it via
xe_dma_buf_move_notify() -> xe_bo_evict(), and the switch dereferences a
NULL resource and faults.

A BO with no resource has nothing placed or mapped, so there is nothing
to evict. Return an empty placement (num_placement = 0), mirroring the
handling already used for non-xe scatter-gather BOs just above;
ttm_bo_validate() then takes the pipeline-gutting path and returns 0.

Without the fix the xe_dma_buf@xe_test_dmabuf_move_notify_no_resource
dynamic live selftest will fail with below stack.

CVE-2026-99685.title: iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure
CVE-2026-99685.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure

viommu_probe() marks the device DRIVER_OK before populating the event
virtqueue and registering the IOMMU device in sysfs. viommu_fill_evtq()
hands the device a set of device-writable buffers through
virtqueue_add_inbuf(), so from that point on the device may write into
them and into the rings.

If either step fails, the error path deletes the virtqueues without
resetting the device first. The event buffers are allocated with
devm_kmalloc_array() and are released as probe unwinds, so the device can
go on writing to memory that has been freed.

Reset the device before deleting the virtqueues, the way viommu_remove()
already does.

CVE-2026-99731.title: mm/filemap: don't lose a folio lock wakeup to a signal
CVE-2026-99731.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/filemap: don't lose a folio lock wakeup to a signal

An exclusive waiter in folio_wait_bit_common() can leave the wait loop
because of a fatal signal, then be woken by folio_unlock() before
finish_wait(). If the waker did not hand over the lock, the waiter returns
-EINTR without trying to acquire it.

folio_wake_bit() stops after waking the first exclusive waiter, so this
loses the wakeup and can leave other waiters asleep indefinitely on an
unlocked folio.

After finish_wait(), let a waiter woken without a lock handoff try once
more to acquire the lock. If successful, return success so the caller's
eventual unlock wakes the next waiter. Otherwise, the current lock owner
will do so.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.
